# Delivery routing ruling (e2e synthetic)

Tanya (team owner) ruled on where reaction delivery belongs:

> we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one
> message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four

Tina pushed back on the batching window and Tanya held: the bundle closes when
the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather
than sending on its own. The alternative considered and rejected was per-skill
delivery with client-side collapsing, which moves the ordering problem onto the
reader.

payload.rationale: I called perspective once and scanned the full map, coverage, and doors. The graph holds no delivery, routing, batching, or run-bundling area; the only areas are the anti-Slack positioning narrative (ungrouped) and the decision-evaporation narrative beneath it, so the document's subject (message batching for reactions) has no direct home. I expanded the Thematic and Documents doors, the anti-Slack narrative, the two active positions (anti-pattern real-time chat, context preservation next sprint), and the decisions-evaporate narrative, since the ruling's motivation (one readable thing instead of fragmented messages) plausibly brushes the real-time-chat anti-pattern and the decision-loss problem. I deliberately did not expand the pricing, target-market, webhook-architecture, or Sprint 4 thesis positions, nor the Tina decision-capture narrative, because they do not bear on batching or delivery routing and would be reaching.
